bigBoard.name: Jeremiah Smith
bigBoard.note: Smith could have All-Pro potential early in his NFL career as a true No. 1 receiver. He immediately changes the offensive outlook for the team that adds him. He is sure-handed and can glide past defenders with ease. And he's equally as capable of winning with strength at the catch point.

bigBoard.name: Leonard Moore
bigBoard.note: With excellent length, speed and technique, Moore is the prototypical cornerback prospect. His length and physicality allow him to excel when getting hands on receivers in press man coverage. He also has the awareness to identify and defend route concepts in zone coverage.

bigBoard.name: Dylan Stewart
bigBoard.note: With a slender frame, Stewart has rare burst and closing speed as a pass rusher. That allows him to wreak havoc on twists and stunts, though the tools have yet to lead to high-end production at the college level.

bigBoard.name: Colin Simmons
bigBoard.note: Simmons is an energetic and high-effort pass rusher, with a quick first step to explode past blockers. He has a nifty combination of hesitation moves and shoulder fakes. But he still needs to develop consistent counter moves, as he can get stuck if his initial move isn't effective.

bigBoard.name: Drew Mestemaker
bigBoard.note: Mestemaker is my top quarterback prospect despite this being only his second season as a starter in high school and college. He has an unconventional style, holding the ball at his waistline before ripping a fiery, three-quarters release.

bigBoard.name: Chris Cole
bigBoard.note: Cole is an easy moving, urgent defender from the second level. He has excellent lateral agility and pursuit speed to close on ball carriers in a hurry. But his ability to read and react to run concepts is still a work in progress, as his eyes can get fixated in the wrong spots.

bigBoard.name: Charlie Becker
bigBoard.note: Becker is primarily used as a vertical threat, and there are few college players who can match his straight-ahead speed. But he is more than just a threat with his legs; he's similar to an NBA rebounder with the way he wins 50-50 passes.

bigBoard.name: Ashton Hampton
bigBoard.note: Hampton is a physically imposing cornerback who strives to humiliate receivers at the line of scrimmage by getting his hands on them. Since most receivers struggle to untangle from his coverage, he would be ideal for press man coverage schemes at the next level.

bigBoard.name: Ellis Robinson IV
bigBoard.note: Robinson is an ultra-athletic cornerback whose quick feet and sudden change of direction helps him stay connected in man coverage. But there are times when Robinson gives up big gains because his technique tends to be abandoned.

bigBoard.name: Will Echoles
bigBoard.note: An explosive 3-technique, Echoles is one of the most versatile and well-conditioned interior defenders in the country. He has energetic hands that help him accelerate past blockers, and reliable lower body strength helps him be a malleable run defender.

bigBoard.name: Jordan Seaton
bigBoard.note: Seaton combines a good blend of awareness, quick hands and lower-body suddenness to be a high-level pass protector. He's also an easy mover in space, which allows him to excel as a puller or on screen plays.

bigBoard.name: Greg Johnson
bigBoard.note: Johnson is a hulking interior blocker whose strength helps him latch and sustain at the point of attack. He has a reliable anchor that helps him tether his feet and quickly stall pass-rush moves. In gap run schemes, Johnson has shown quickness when pulling.

bigBoard.name: CJ Carr
bigBoard.note: Carr is a refined pocket passer whose eyes, feet and throwing motion are always in cohesion. With an easy throwing motion, he is a decisive passer who trusts his eyes to pick apart defenses. He has a great feel for the types of passes that are needed, putting enough touch or velocity on them.

bigBoard.name: Xavier Gilliam
bigBoard.note: Gilliam is an explosive, upfield interior defender who can penetrate the first level with ease. His game centers around quickness, as his first step is difficult for blockers to match. Gilliam's active hands help him win with multiple plans of attack in pass-rush situations.

bigBoard.name: Zereoue Williams
bigBoard.note: Williams' playing style is a bit unconventional, and his lack of experience shows throughout games. However, he has plenty of skills that NFL teams covet. Williams' towering frame helps him shadow and shut down pass rushers around the arc of the pocket.

bigBoard.name: Austin Simmons
bigBoard.note: Simmons has a slight build but is an extremely explosive thrower with A-level arm strength. His baseball pitching background shows, as he has a whippy and violent throwing motion that adds excellent velocity to his passes.

bigBoard.name: Jackson Harris
bigBoard.note: Harris is a sudden, smooth route runner who can execute any branch on the route tree. He can maneuver and control defenders by executing efficient steps and extra body moves.

bigBoard.name: Darian Mensah
bigBoard.note: Mensah is a locate-and-loft thrower who has a great sense of true progressions and can string together long stretches of accurate completions. He has great touch on passes, as he can drop throws right into the outstretched arms of targets.

bigBoard.name: Nick Marsh
bigBoard.note: Built like a running back, Marsh's separators are his frame, competitiveness and power at the catch point. His strong releases at the line help him work through and steer clear of press coverage prior to making catches.

bigBoard.name: Jamari Johnson
bigBoard.note: Johnson is a big playmaker in the passing game, especially over the middle of the field. He has natural hands and the catch radius to pluck balls outside his frame. As a route runner, Johnson wins with controlled tempos, decisiveness and spatial awareness.

bigBoard.name: Trevor Lauck
bigBoard.note: Lauck is an old-school, tough offensive tackle. His playing style isn't flashy or glamorous; he simply collects wins in bunches by executing his hand power and physicality. Lauck has upper-tier upper-body strength and hands that are active when initiating contact.

bigBoard.name: Lance Heard
bigBoard.note: Heard is a physical, wide-framed blocker who uses his natural tools effectively. His physicality is always turned up to the max, as he seeks to destroy anything in his path as a true road grader.

bigBoard.name: Boubacar Traore
bigBoard.note: Traore is a long, disruptive presence off the edge. He displays an expansive repertoire of pass-rush moves, including effective speed-to-power transitions and timely spin moves. He has a nonstop motor, routinely accelerates around the rim of pockets and has the bending ability to turn the corner.

bigBoard.name: Devan Thompkins
bigBoard.note: Thompkins is a heavy handed, versatile defender capable of rushing from inside and off the edge. With upper-level hand power, he can stack and shed from blockers with ease.

bigBoard.name: LaNorris Sellers
bigBoard.note: Sellers is an explosive dual-threat passer with A-level arm power, mobility and body strength. He has a great feel for trajectory and touch on long passes and can make "drop it in the bucket" throws downfield. His compact release helps him fire the ball into condensed windows in intermediate areas.

bigBoard.name: Trey'Dez Green
bigBoard.note: Green is like an NBA small forward on the turf, constantly presenting a tall task for defenses. As a true "F" tight end, he's a movable offensive weapon who provides most of value as a pass catcher from the slot or split out wide.

bigBoard.name: Yhonzae Pierre
bigBoard.note: Pierre is an aggressive defender whose pursuit energy has very little drop-off throughout games. He is equally as effective from a stand-up outside linebacker position or with his hand in the ground. Pierre is a true havoc creator on stunts and twists, using overwhelming strength to get blockers.

bigBoard.name: Jadan Baugh
bigBoard.note: Baugh is the top running back prospect in this class, a chiseled and powerful runner with timely short-area quickness. He activates his lower body to slither his way through creases, while also being able to simply plant his foot and accelerate through the line of scrimmage.

bigBoard.name: Kelley Jones
bigBoard.note: Jones is a slender corner who has shielding length on the perimeter. His angular build helps him excel in coverage, where he can utilize his frame on a vertical plane. Jones has good hips and vertical speed to stay hip-to-hip with receivers.

bigBoard.name: KJ Bolden
bigBoard.note: Bolden plays a variety of spots in Georgia's secondary but projects best as a center field free safety. He is a mistake eraser in the back end, showcasing range and instinctiveness to quickly bring a halt to plays. Bolden is an aggressive tackler who comes downhill with urgency.

bigBoard.name: Cam Coleman
bigBoard.note: A lanky and long-striding target, Coleman is a no-nonsense route runner who quickly drives off the line of scrimmage when given free releases. He has routine hands and an extended catch radius that help him snatch the ball out of the air regardless of where it's located.

bigBoard.name: Trevor Goosby
bigBoard.note: Goosby has a gangly build for a tackle prospect, which gives him excellent length to match and mirror defenders off the edge. His hand power and timing allow him to generate movement at the point of attack.

bigBoard.name: Arch Manning
bigBoard.note: Manning has prototypical size and a well-built frame for the position. His arm strength provides exciting plays when throwing to the intermediate and deep portions of the field, and his above-average mobility allows him to take off when defenses leave an opening.

bigBoard.name: Kade Pieper
bigBoard.note: Pieper is a highly competitive interior blocker, with the core strength to challenge the desire of down linemen. Winning with angles, he has an innate feel to beat defenders to spots on zone concepts prior to initiating contact.

bigBoard.name: Dante Moore
bigBoard.note: From his footwork to throwing release, Moore is a natural in every area for the position. He orchestrates Oregon's up-tempo attack efficiently with B-level arm strength. His game is predicated upon rhythm, timing and anticipation, showing comfort with concepts to all levels of the field.

bigBoard.name: Trinidad Chambliss
bigBoard.note: A headache for the opposition in multiple ways, Chambliss can break down defenses with both his throwing ability and mobility. His excellent field vision complements a compact and fiery release, helping him anticipate and attack over the middle.
